generator.params.bud_area.note: The leaf area its `bud` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows: the bud is now its flower closed, where before it drew the fruit ovoid.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Mimulus guttatus: stems 40 cm to 1 m tall. The typical value is the one the plant was drawn at before, inside the source's range.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Mimulus guttatus: leaves 1.5 cm to 9 cm long.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a lush herb of seeps and stream edges with round, toothed leaves in pairs and snapdragon-like yellow flowers spotted red in the throat. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.4 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green leaves; yellow flowers. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): a yellow two-lipped tube of five joined petals, five sepals, four stamens and a superior pistil of two carpels, from the characters of Phrymaceae by the rules at the flowering plants.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.zygomorphy.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 422, Erythranthe guttata: zygomorphy bilabiate, open throat.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
